name: London System
description: A simple d4 setup course that teaches the default London structure first, then common Black reactions.

branches.title: Main Line: London Setup
branches.description: Learn the basic London starting pattern.

moves.title: Start with d4
moves.explanation: Controls e5 and c5, opens the c1 bishop, and gives White a stable central base.

moves.title: Black mirrors
moves.explanation: Black also takes central space. The position is stable enough for a setup approach.

moves.title: Develop bishop outside
moves.explanation: Bf4 develops the bishop before e3 can block it. This is the key London habit.

hints: The target response in this branch is Bf4.
Use the highlighted move and keep the plan simple.

branches.title: Normal Development Response
branches.description: If Black develops a knight, continue the London setup.

moves.title: Black develops
moves.explanation: Black controls e4 and d5 with a knight.

moves.title: Recommended: Bf4
moves.explanation: Develop the bishop outside the pawn chain and keep the setup simple.

hints: The target response in this branch is Bf4.
Use the highlighted move and keep the plan simple.
coachingNotes: If Black develops a knight, continue the London setup.

branches.title: Center Challenge Response
branches.description: If Black attacks d4 with c5, support the center.

moves.title: Black challenges
moves.explanation: Black attacks d4 from the side.

moves.title: Recommended: support and develop
moves.explanation: e3 supports the center and opens the f1 bishop. Keep developing instead of grabbing pawns too soon.

hints: The target response in this branch is e3.
Use the highlighted move and keep the plan simple.

branches.title: Fianchetto Response
branches.description: If Black prepares a bishop on g7, build normally.

moves.title: Recommended: keep the setup
moves.explanation: Bf4 develops before e3 and keeps your plan consistent.
